title: Bharat Value Fund bets ₹300 crore for undisclosed stake in Big Mishra Pedha - The HinduBusinessLine
text:
Bharat Value Fund, a private equity vehicle, on Tuesday announced a ₹300 crore investment in Big Mishra Pedha for an undisclosed stake.

The company operates over 200 outlets in North Karnataka, Goa and southern Maharashtra. It is aiming to transition into a national food platform from a regional heritage brand, an official statement said, adding that the investment will help realise this aspiration.

Big Mishra, a 93-year-old brand, is the custodian of the GI-tagged 'Dharwad Pedha' and plans to add 100 outlets and enter over 50 new cities in the next two years, supported by modern trade and quick commerce expansion, it said.

The company's revenues have more than doubled to ₹300 crore in FY26 from ₹142 crore in FY22, the statement said, adding that the pre-tax profitability is healthy.

It serves over a crore customers each year and operates two state-of-the-art manufacturing facilities and an in-house dairy.

Bharat Value Fund is a category II alternate investment fund promoted by 'The Wealth Company', which is focused on identifying and scaling high-potential Indian businesses.

The Wealth Company Asset Management founder Madhu Lunawat said many strong regional brands have not yet had the opportunity to scale nationally despite earning consumer trust.

“We believe our role is to help such regional champions scale while retaining the heritage and entrepreneurial strengths that made them successful in the first place,” she added.

BVF brings institutional capital, strategic expertise and governance framework required for the next phase of growth, while allowing it to preserve the heritage and quality that have defined Dharwad Pedha for generations, the company's promoter Sanjay Ganesh Mishra said.
